title: Which sources are lawfully and technically reachable per region, and what changes by jurisdiction?

unreachable_only_source_plan.catalog_retry_policy_verbatim_shape: two strikes then pivot; switch source class (official doc -> source code -> issue tracker -> archive) before a third attempt; hard stop at 4 total, then emit a proof-of-impossibility record
do: record the barrier class with HTTP status or block-page bytes + sha256 + timestamp
re-run the detector control URL in the same process; if control fails, park as detector-failure
after 2 failures on the same route fingerprint, pivot source class: official-docs -> source-code -> issue-tracker -> archival
hard stop at 4 total attempts, then emit a proof-of-impossibility record
label the claim UNREACHABLE / NOT-CHECKED; it MUST NOT gate a decision
set revalidation expiry: 7d for WAF/bot, 30d for geo, until-owner-gate for legal/Tor
if an archive copy is used, label it source_class=archival (not a live equivalent)
do_not: infer the missing content from a policy, block, or paywall page
enable Tor / fetch .onion (that is RES-0119, owner-gated)
bypass WAF, login, paywall, or robots Disallow (access-control bypass)
treat a WAF 403 as proof the source does not exist
mark the claim CONFIRMED from a single blocked fetch
unreachable_only_source_plan.falsifier_for_this_plan: A later fetch of the same URL from this same egress returning HTTP 2xx with the claimed content, while the detector control still succeeds, overturns an UNREACHABLE verdict for that URL.
